risks: Our 100% dependency on carriers for cargo transportation exposes us to risks related to capacity availability, cost fluctuations, and service disruptions.
Our entire revenue is dependent upon the availability of the carriers and any disruption will materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.
Any disruption in these primary services may therefore adversely impact our overall operational results.
Additionally, volatility in fuel prices and exchange rate fluctuations influences our cost structure, particularly when rising transportation costs cannot be fully or promptly passed on to customers.
Especially for air freight forwarding vertical, our Company does not charter any capacity and rather secures appropriate space on back-to-back basis after receiving confirmation from the customer.
These arrangements are essential for ensuring reliable and timely transportation of goods from one location to another and form a critical component of our service offerings to customers.

Our ability to secure, maintain and renew such agreements on commercially viable terms is subject to various factors including commercial negotiations, strategic priorities of such airlines, changes in industry dynamics, regulatory constraints, and availability of cargo capacity.
Limited cargo capacity especially during peak demand periods or global supply chain disruptions may restrict our ability to secure space at competitive rates.

business_ops.seasonality: Disclosed qualitatively in the MD&A 'Key Factors That May Affect Our Results of Services', with no quantified quarterly split. Verbatim: 'In addition, our business is subject to seasonal fluctuations, with certain periods seeing higher volumes due to festivals, inventory cycles, or export deadlines. These seasonal factors can contribute to variability in our operating performance across quarters.' And: 'We are also subject to the seasonal nature of trade activity. Certain periods, such as pre-festive seasons or financial year-end cycles, typically see increased cargo movement, while others may reflect lower volumes. These fluctuations in demand affect the utilisation of our infrastructure and resources and may lead to variations in our operational and financial performance across quarters.'
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: The Company describes a deliberate backward-and-forward integration strategy executed through subsidiaries rather than owned transport assets. Stated verbatim in Our Business: 'In response to the evolving dynamics and increasing competitiveness of the global freight forwarding industry, our company adopted a proactive strategy aimed at enhancing operational efficiency, broadening market access, and delivering comprehensive, integrated logistics solutions to our customers through a combination of backward and forward integration. To support this strategic vision, our company incorporated and acquired multiple subsidiary entities, both within India and across key international markets.' In Business Strategies: 'As a comprehensive logistics solutions provider, we strategically leverage both backward and forward integration to optimize cost efficiencies and streamline service delivery across the supply chain. By internalizing critical functions such as last-mile delivery and customer support, we significantly reduce reliance on external courier services and call centre providers, thereby eliminating associated fees while ensuring a consistently high standard of service reliability and responsiveness. This end-to-end control over upstream procurement and downstream distribution operations enables us to retain greater revenue within the organization...' The group comprises 17 Indian subsidiaries, 6 foreign subsidiaries and 6 step-down subsidiaries, each with a specific mandate: warehousing (Skyways SLS Logistik Pvt Ltd), road transportation (Phantom Road Express Pvt Ltd), technology platforms (sGate Tech Solutions Pvt Ltd 51%, SLS ASAP Tech Systems Pvt Ltd), LCL ocean consolidation (Hubload SLS Services Pvt Ltd), tech-driven express door-to-door cargo and courier (Skart Global Express Pvt Ltd 95%), logistics skill development (SLS Logistik Academy Pvt Ltd 90%), e-commerce retail and digital marketing (SLS Retail Supermart Pvt Ltd 90%), ocean and warehousing (Forin Container Line Pvt Ltd 82.27%), cross-border freight forwarding (Surgeport Logistics Pvt Ltd 76%, Brace Port Logistics Ltd 51.09%), and specialised pharma/automotive ocean and air logistics (Odyssey Logistics Pvt Ltd 51%), plus international freight forwarding subsidiaries in Germany, Hong Kong, Dubai, Vietnam, Cambodia, the UK, the UAE, the USA, Canada and Saudi Arabia. Upstream, the model remains asset-light and carrier-dependent: 'We rely extensively on third-party carriers for the transportation of cargo, as we do not operate our own aircraft or shipping lines. Consequently, our business is 100% dependent on the availability, pricing, and service quality of such carriers.' Forward integration into infrastructure is proposed but not yet operational - the Company has undertaken a strategic initiative to expand into management and maintenance of cargo terminals (air and ocean), CFS, ICDs, logistics parks, industrial parks, warehousing complexes, cold storage facilities, freight corridors and dry ports, and has bid jointly with Swissport International AG for a DBFOT cargo terminal at Kolkata airport.

record_gaps: Form-2 relating to the allotment of 4,276 equity shares on June 12, 1986 is not traceable. Risk Factor 36 states: "Our Company has not been able to trace Form-2 related to the allotment of 4,276 equity shares on dated June 12, 1986. Despite undertaking an extensive search of our available records, these documents could not be located." The Company has relied on a certificate issued by M/s. S.K. Joshi & Associates, Practicing Company Secretary, together with alternative documentation - the Memorandum of Association, minutes of Board and shareholder meetings, the Register of Members and subsequent filings and financial statements. Critically, the RHP states that "no additional compliance-related filings in respect of these allotments could be traced, either in our internal records or those of the Registrar of Companies", so the Company "cannot confirm whether such filings were made in accordance with applicable law, were made at all, or were filed within the prescribed timelines". No penalties or regulatory actions have been imposed in connection with these missing records as at the date of the RHP.

Audit trail (edit log) instances: the FY2026 auditors' report carves out "the instances discussed in note 52 to the consolidated financial statements" from its Rule 11(g) assertion, and the FY2025 report carves out the instances in note 50. Those instances are, by definition, periods or transactions for which the edit log did not operate - a record-traceability gap in the accounting software itself. The substance of notes 52 and 50 is not recoverable from the material available: both notes sit inside the restated annexure at RHP pdf pp.374-474, which is a scanned image, and neither note was captured in the OCR pass around the related-party disclosures. A reviewer should obtain notes 52 and 50 from the source PDF to establish which entities, which periods and which transaction classes lacked an operative audit trail.

opportunities: E-commerce Expansion: The rapid rise of e-commerce in India has escalated demand for quick and reliable delivery, which air cargo is uniquely positioned to meet.

Government Initiatives: Policies focused on modernizing infrastructure, streamlining regulations and promoting public-private partnerships are set to enhance the efficiency and capacity of air cargo operations.

Investment in Infrastructure: Ongoing and planned investment in airport infrastructure, dedicated cargo terminals and integrated logistics parks presents an opportunity to alleviate current bottlenecks.
Regional Trade Agreements: India's participation in regional trade agreements can open new markets and increase cargo volumes through enhanced cross-border air cargo movement.
swot.scope_note: This is the RHP's own section headed 'INDUSTRY SWOT ANALYSIS' in the Industry Overview chapter (sourced to the D&B Report dated July 17, 2026). It is an INDUSTRY-level SWOT for Indian logistics with emphasis on airways logistics — it is NOT a company-specific SWOT of Skyways Air Services Limited, and the RHP prints no company SWOT.
strengths: Strategic Geographic Position: India's central location in South Asia positions it as a crucial hub for international trade routes connecting East and West, facilitating efficient distribution channels for domestic and international markets.

Robust Economic Growth: India's consistent economic expansion drives demand for sophisticated logistics services, making timely and reliable transportation, especially via air freight, increasingly critical.

Expanding Air Cargo Market: The Indian air cargo market reached approximately USD 13.44 billion in 2024, with a projected CAGR of 5.80% between 2025 and 2034, potentially attaining USD 23.62 billion by 2034.
Technological Integration: Adoption of automation, real-time tracking and data analytics has enhanced operational efficiency, improving cargo handling and reducing turnaround times.
threats: Intense Competition: The air cargo sector faces stiff competition from road, rail and sea, which may be more cost-effective for certain cargo, while international carriers operating in India add further competitive pressure.
Environmental Concerns: The carbon footprint of air freight is under increasing scrutiny; emission-reduction and sustainability regulation could impose additional costs and operational constraints.
Global Economic Fluctuations: The industry is vulnerable to global economic downturns, trade restrictions and geopolitical tensions that disrupt supply chains and reduce trade volumes.
Pandemic and Health Crises: Health crises such as COVID-19 have demonstrated potential for severe disruption through travel restrictions, reduced flight frequencies and labour shortages.
weaknesses: Infrastructure Limitations: Many Indian airports face inadequate cargo handling facilities, limited warehousing space and outdated equipment, causing delays and increasing operational costs.
Regulatory Challenges: Complex customs procedures and bureaucratic hurdles impede swift movement of goods; lengthy clearance processes diminish the speed advantage of air freight.
High Operational Costs: Air freight is inherently more expensive than other modes, with volatile fuel prices, high airport charges and maintenance expenses deterring price-sensitive customers.
Limited Domestic Connectivity: Regional connectivity remains underdeveloped relative to major metropolitan areas, restricting the reach of air cargo services in remote or underserved regions.

overview.business_model: The Company earns revenue by buying and reselling cargo capacity and by charging for the logistics services wrapped around it. It does not own aircraft or shipping lines: it books space with third-party carriers on a back-to-back basis after receiving customer confirmation and bills the customer for the movement, so revenue is recognised gross on the freight while carrier cost sits in cost of services. In FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 2,81,289.89 lakhs was 77.02% Air Cargo Services (Rs 2,16,639.87 lakhs), 15.02% Ocean Cargo Services (Rs 42,260.32 lakhs), 5.79% Express Cargo and Parcel (Rs 16,277.96 lakhs), 1.38% Trucking, 0.61% Value Added Services, 0.13% Warehousing and 0.05% sale of products (E-commerce and other retail). Customs broking, warehousing, trucking, technology-driven express/parcel delivery and value-added services are sold alongside the forwarding business; the technology subsidiary sGate Tech Solutions Private Limited builds the proprietary booking, tracking and workflow platforms used across the group. Group scale is delivered through Indian and overseas subsidiaries and associates, several of which are not wholly owned - non-controlling interests were Rs 16,209.31 lakhs of total equity of Rs 49,473.52 lakhs at March 31, 2026.

genesis.founding_story: The Company began its operations as a Custom House Agent (CHA), now known as a Custom Broker licence holder, and progressively expanded its service offerings over the years in response to evolving market requirements and international trade dynamics. The initial subscription to the Memorandum of Association on December 21, 1984 was two equity shares of face value Rs 100 each, one each to Sudershan Lal Sharma and Manohar Lal Sharma. Over four decades the Company moved beyond air freight forwarding and customs broking into a multi-modal logistics provider spanning ocean freight forwarding, trucking, warehousing, technology-driven express cargo and parcel delivery and value-added services, building out the group through Indian and overseas subsidiaries.

concerns_observed: Basic and diluted EPS FELL from Rs 3.71 (FY25) to Rs 3.56 (FY26) even though consolidated PAT rose 32% from Rs 4,813.97 to Rs 6,352.38 lakhs, because profit attributable to non-controlling interests went from Rs 897.11 to Rs 2,251.50 lakhs and paid-up capital rose to Rs 11,644.52 lakhs; non-controlling interests are Rs 16,209.31 lakhs of total equity of Rs 49,473.52 lakhs, so a third of the group's equity - and a rising share of its profit - does not belong to the parent.

A material part of the Rs 13,000.00 lakh working-capital Object funds a change in supplier-payment policy rather than growth: the FY27 working-capital gap is projected to jump 80.99% (Rs 31,107.09 to Rs 56,300.54 lakhs) against 31.22% actual growth in FY26, and trade payables are projected to FALL from Rs 21,156.74 to Rs 13,080.00 lakhs with payable days going 50 to 34 to 20, disclosed as deliberately 'reduced dependence on supplier credit'.

Unit economics deteriorated on both legs in FY26 while volumes grew: average air freight realisation fell from Rs 280 to Rs 258 per kg (-7.88%) and average ocean realisation from Rs 1,80,436 to Rs 1,49,462 per TEU (-18.79%); the Company also states that in FY24 lower freight rates cut turnover versus the prior fiscal.

The model is structurally thin and debt-funded: a 2.26% PAT margin on Rs 2,81,289.89 lakhs of revenue, against total debt of Rs 62,405.68 lakhs and a finance cost of Rs 4,807.64 lakhs that consumes 38% of FY26 EBITDA of Rs 12,564.86 lakhs; the working-capital gap was funded by working capital loans to the extent of 86.23% (FY26), 100.00% (FY25) and 82.62% (FY24).

The jump in pharmaceuticals from 7.27% to 9.11% to 22.89% of revenue is acquisition-driven, not organic - the RHP's own client-table footnote states Odyssey Logistics Private Limited was acquired with effect from 1 February 2025 and revenue is counted only post-acquisition, and named pharma clients (Cipla, J B Chemicals, Serum Institute, Torrent Pharma) appear only from that point.

A majority of the 18 subsidiaries in the RHP's own loss table posted a loss in FY26, including Skart Global Express Rs 450.91 lakhs, Phantom Road Express Rs 298.55 lakhs, SLS Retail Supermart Rs 273.70 lakhs and Skyways SLS Cargo Services LLC UAE Rs 160.30 lakhs - the same entity set the holding company guarantees.

Audit scope across the group is fragmented: the statutory auditors did not audit 12, 10 and 2 subsidiaries in FY26, FY25 and FY24 respectively (FY26 other-auditor entities: total assets Rs 12,305.73 lakhs, total revenue Rs 37,870.68 lakhs), and 4 subsidiaries for FY24 were not audited at all (total assets Rs 4,707.62 lakhs, total revenue Rs 7,843.08 lakhs).

red_flags: FIR No. 0172 of 2025 dated 12 December 2025 at the Economic Offences Wing, Delhi names the COMPANY ITSELF as Accused No. 3 and Material Subsidiary Brace Port Logistics Limited as Accused No. 2 among nine accused, on a complaint by PG Paper Company Limited (UK) alleging criminal breach of trust, cheating, fake documents, inflated freight invoicing and bribery of the main accused, with an alleged direct loss of not less than Rs 4,420 lakhs; and it has already crystallised into an operating-licence loss - the Authorized Economic Operator LO certificate (INAABCS3895B0F255) has been SUSPENDED with effect from 4 May 2026 with revocation proposed, pending after the Company's 28 July 2026 response, with no assurance as to when it will be revoked. The RHP's own exculpatory position must be carried with this: it states there were no direct transactions between the Company and the complainant (the dealings were the subsidiaries'), the Company replied on 13 February 2026 to the police notice stating it is not involved in day-to-day operations or execution and would cooperate, it holds 51.09% (not the 80% alleged) of Brace Port which is separately listed on NSE EMERGE and independently managed with the Company's directors serving only as non-executives, and the FIR was NOT registered for the PMLA or FEMA offences the complaint referred to.

Operating cash flow has repeatedly failed to track reported profit: CFO was Rs 201.05 lakhs in FY25 against PAT of Rs 4,813.97 lakhs and NEGATIVE Rs 904.17 lakhs in FY24 against PAT of Rs 3,449.35 lakhs, before recovering to Rs 11,361.60 lakhs in FY26. Trade receivables stand at Rs 57,947.65 lakhs against revenue of Rs 2,81,289.89 lakhs (75 debtor days), FY24's deficit is attributed by the RHP to a Rs 14,482.08 lakh increase in receivables, and investing cash flow was negative in all three years (Rs 13,101.29 / 15,228.95 / 17,911.15 lakhs) with the gap funded by financing inflows of Rs 15,534.08 / 22,148.70 / 5,208.21 lakhs.

Auditor findings are repeating and widening rather than one-off: CARO-qualified or adverse entities went from 2 (FY24) to 13 (FY25) to 14 (FY26), and the HOLDING COMPANY itself carries the identical five clauses - i(c), ii(b), iii(c), vii(b) and ix(f) - in both FY26 and FY25, up from two clauses in FY24. The Rule 11(g) audit-trail modification recurs in all three years (notes 52, 50 and 54), and the RHP prints only the clause numbers, never the substance of any qualification, so a reader cannot size a single one of them.

Contingent liabilities and commitments of Rs 28,908.02 lakhs equal 86.90% of parent net worth of Rs 33,264.21 lakhs at 31 March 2026, and are dominated by corporate guarantees the holding company has issued for subsidiaries - Forin Container Line Rs 13,507.90 lakhs, Phantom Express Rs 4,065.00 lakhs, Skart Global Express Rs 2,000.00 lakhs, Skyways SLS Cargo Services LLC UAE Rs 1,656.45 lakhs, Brace Port Rs 1,000.00 lakhs, Rahat Continental Rs 1,000.00 lakhs and Skyways SLS Logistik GMBH Rs 654.00 lakhs - while a majority of the 18 subsidiaries in the RHP's own table lost money in FY26, including three of the guaranteed entities (Skart Global Express Rs 450.91 lakhs, Phantom Road Express Rs 298.55 lakhs, Skyways SLS Cargo Services LLC UAE Rs 160.30 lakhs).

Promoters Yashpal Sharma and Tarun Sharma, together with a Promoter Group member, personally guarantee Rs 74,563 lakhs of the Rs 79,536.68 lakhs of secured borrowings sanctioned as at 30 June 2026 - 93.75% of sanctioned limits - and residential properties of the Promoters have been mortgaged as security, while the Debt Service Coverage Ratio has fallen from 3.15x (FY24) to 2.45x (FY25) to 1.48x (FY26). The RHP records no historical default in principal or interest, attributing a few NACH failures to technical reasons rather than insufficiency of funds.

FY26 introduced related-party dealings with no prior-year comparative: a Rs 1,823.79 lakh line captioned 'Purchase of Property, plant and equipment', being Rs 900.00 lakhs each with Yashpal Sharma and Tarun Sharma plus Rs 23.79 lakhs with Vinod Sharma, and a Rs 50.49 lakh trade receivable from Yashpal Sharma at 31 March 2026 that was nil at both 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024. The RHP states related-party transactions are on an arms' length basis but prints no valuation, terms or counterparty rationale for either item.

Statutory-record hygiene is poor across a long period: 47 tabulated instances of delayed RoC filing over FY24 to the RHP date, with DPT-3 delayed up to 347 days, MGT-14 for sweat-equity approval up to 217 days, ADT-1 for auditor appointment 207 days, SH-7 199 days and CHG-1 satisfaction of charge up to 194 days, described by the RHP itself as including non-compliances 'some of which may not be rectifiable under applicable laws'; Form-2 for the 12 June 1986 allotment of 4,276 shares is untraceable and the Company cannot confirm whether the related filings were ever made; and FEMA reporting is outstanding on three fronts - Form FC-GPR for 5,07,711 shares allotted to a non-resident, Form FC-TRS for transfers by Whole-Time Directors Himanshu Chhabra and Rohit Sehgal (an obligation the RHP records rests on the resident transferors, who would bear any RBI penalty), and the Annual Performance Report for subsidiary Odyssey Logistics Private Limited's Rs 44.89 lakh 2018 overseas investment, which the RHP records as attributable to the Subsidiary and as predating the Company's January 2025 acquisition of it.
strengths_observed: Revenue more than doubled in two years, from Rs 1,28,911.01 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 2,24,782.49 lakhs (FY25) to Rs 2,81,289.89 lakhs (FY26), and EBITDA rose faster still - Rs 4,834.42 to Rs 8,648.86 to Rs 12,564.86 lakhs - so the EBITDA margin widened from 3.75% to 3.85% to 4.47% even as per-unit realisations fell.

Growth was volume-led against falling prices, which is consistent with share gain rather than price-taking: air cargo handled rose from 48,013.16 tonnes (FY24) to 83,923.81 tonnes (FY26) and ocean from 16,294 to 28,275 TEU, while air realisation fell 7.88% to Rs 258 per kg and ocean realisation fell 18.79% to Rs 1,49,462 per TEU in FY26.

Operating cash flow turned firmly positive in FY26 at Rs 11,361.60 lakhs against PAT of Rs 6,352.38 lakhs, after Rs 201.05 lakhs in FY25 and negative Rs 904.17 lakhs in FY24 - the first year in the restated record in which CFO exceeded reported profit.

Customer concentration is low for the sector: top-5 customers were 14.04% and top-10 20.69% of FY26 revenue from operations (FY25: 8.03% / 11.57%), across a stated base of 9,504 customers, and no top-5 or top-10 supplier was lost in FY26, FY25 or FY24.

Both rating agencies upgraded during the period and neither has downgraded in three fiscals: CRISIL moved from A-/Positive to A/Stable on 05.03.2025 (reaffirmed 02.06.2026 on Rs 23,010.00 lakhs of long-term fund-based facilities) and CARE from A-/Positive to A/Stable on 07.04.2025 (reaffirmed 09.04.2026 on Rs 22,100.00 lakhs).

The air-side model carries no fixed capacity obligation - the Company charters no capacity and books space on a back-to-back basis only after customer confirmation - supported by relationships with 56 airlines in FY26 (44 in FY24) and performance-based agreements with Emirates, Saudi Cargo, Air India Cargo and Lufthansa.

Workforce and statutory-payment hygiene improved on the Company's own certified tables: attrition fell from 43.66% (FY24) to 31.23% (FY25) to 18.73% (FY26), and professional-tax delay instances fell from 30 (FY24) to 14 (FY25) to 4 (FY26).

Capital structure is uncomplicated as at the RHP date: one class of shares, all fully paid, no outstanding convertibles, warrants, options or ESOP/ESPS, no corporate promoter, Promoter Group holding nil, and an affirmative statement that none of the Promoters' shares are pledged (Capital Structure, page 103).

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company describes a deliberate backward-and-forward integration strategy executed through subsidiaries rather than owned transport assets. Stated verbatim in Our Business: 'In response to the evolving dynamics and increasing competitiveness of the global freight forwarding industry, our company adopted a proactive strategy aimed at enhancing operational efficiency, broadening market access, and delivering comprehensive, integrated logistics solutions to our customers through a combination of backward and forward integration. To support this strategic vision, our company incorporated and acquired multiple subsidiary entities, both within India and across key international markets.' In Business Strategies: 'As a comprehensive logistics solutions provider, we strategically leverage both backward and forward integration to optimize cost efficiencies and streamline service delivery across the supply chain. By internalizing critical functions such as last-mile delivery and customer support, we significantly reduce reliance on external courier services and call centre providers, thereby eliminating associated fees while ensuring a consistently high standard of service reliability and responsiveness. This end-to-end control over upstream procurement and downstream distribution operations enables us to retain greater revenue within the organization...' The group comprises 17 Indian subsidiaries, 6 foreign subsidiaries and 6 step-down subsidiaries, each with a specific mandate: warehousing (Skyways SLS Logistik Pvt Ltd), road transportation (Phantom Road Express Pvt Ltd), technology platforms (sGate Tech Solutions Pvt Ltd 51%, SLS ASAP Tech Systems Pvt Ltd), LCL ocean consolidation (Hubload SLS Services Pvt Ltd), tech-driven express door-to-door cargo and courier (Skart Global Express Pvt Ltd 95%), logistics skill development (SLS Logistik Academy Pvt Ltd 90%), e-commerce retail and digital marketing (SLS Retail Supermart Pvt Ltd 90%), ocean and warehousing (Forin Container Line Pvt Ltd 82.27%), cross-border freight forwarding (Surgeport Logistics Pvt Ltd 76%, Brace Port Logistics Ltd 51.09%), and specialised pharma/automotive ocean and air logistics (Odyssey Logistics Pvt Ltd 51%), plus international freight forwarding subsidiaries in Germany, Hong Kong, Dubai, Vietnam, Cambodia, the UK, the UAE, the USA, Canada and Saudi Arabia. Upstream, the model remains asset-light and carrier-dependent: 'We rely extensively on third-party carriers for the transportation of cargo, as we do not operate our own aircraft or shipping lines. Consequently, our business is 100% dependent on the availability, pricing, and service quality of such carriers.' Forward integration into infrastructure is proposed but not yet operational - the Company has undertaken a strategic initiative to expand into management and maintenance of cargo terminals (air and ocean), CFS, ICDs, logistics parks, industrial parks, warehousing complexes, cold storage facilities, freight corridors and dry ports, and has bid jointly with Swissport International AG for a DBFOT cargo terminal at Kolkata airport.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Disclosed qualitatively in the MD&A 'Key Factors That May Affect Our Results of Services', with no quantified quarterly split. Verbatim: 'In addition, our business is subject to seasonal fluctuations, with certain periods seeing higher volumes due to festivals, inventory cycles, or export deadlines. These seasonal factors can contribute to variability in our operating performance across quarters.' And: 'We are also subject to the seasonal nature of trade activity. Certain periods, such as pre-festive seasons or financial year-end cycles, typically see increased cargo movement, while others may reflect lower volumes. These fluctuations in demand affect the utilisation of our infrastructure and resources and may lead to variations in our operational and financial performance across quarters.'

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Our 100% dependency on carriers for cargo transportation exposes us to risks related to capacity availability, cost fluctuations, and service disruptions.
- Our entire revenue is dependent upon the availability of the carriers and any disruption will materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.
- Any disruption in these primary services may therefore adversely impact our overall operational results.
- Additionally, volatility in fuel prices and exchange rate fluctuations influences our cost structure, particularly when rising transportation costs cannot be fully or promptly passed on to customers.
- Especially for air freight forwarding vertical, our Company does not charter any capacity and rather secures appropriate space on back-to-back basis after receiving confirmation from the customer.
- These arrangements are essential for ensuring reliable and timely transportation of goods from one location to another and form a critical component of our service offerings to customers.
- Our ability to secure, maintain and renew such agreements on commercially viable terms is subject to various factors including commercial negotiations, strategic priorities of such airlines, changes in industry dynamics, regulatory constraints, and availability of cargo capacity.
- Limited cargo capacity especially during peak demand periods or global supply chain disruptions may restrict our ability to secure space at competitive rates.
